persona.label: Rushed but qualified
persona.description: Busy professional between meetings. Terse, answers several things at once. Should be transferred.
persona.behavior: You are between meetings and have about five minutes. Your first reply says something like "ok but make it fast, I'm busy." Use short, lowercase texts with no pleasantries. When asked something, answer it, and volunteer one or two related facts if it saves time. Round numbers the way people do ("about 520", "owe like 310k"). If the assistant is slow or repetitive, show mild impatience. You want a lower rate and you want to talk to someone today.

transcript.text: Hi Taylor, this is Riley, an automated assistant with Harborline Home Loans. I'm following up on the refinance inquiry you just sent us. Is now a good time for a few quick questions? You can reply STOP at any time.
ok but make it fast, i'm busy. looking to lower my rate, currently at 7.25
Got it, I'll keep it quick. Roughly what's your home worth today? A ballpark is fine.

callback.notes: Taylor Brooks, busy until 4. Rate-and-term refi, wants to lower rate from 7.25%. Primary residence, home value ~$520k, balance ~$310k, self-reported credit 740+. Timeline ASAP. All intake fields collected.

objections.rationale: The borrower said "ok but make it fast, i'm busy," which signaled they would answer by text now. The agent replied "Got it, I'll keep it quick" and kept each question to one line. It never explicitly offered the callback alternative from the playbook, but it honored the borrower's choice and booked a callback when asked in [7].

judge.naturalness_rationale: Messages are brief, warm, and one question at a time, which suits a busy borrower. Examples: "A ballpark is fine," "Last one:". The agent adapted when the borrower volunteered extra info: it skipped asking for balance after [3] and credit after [5].
judge.experience_rationale: The intake was fast, with no repetition, and the agent skipped questions the borrower had already answered ([4], [6]). In [8] it set a clear expectation: "A licensed loan officer will call you at this number" "today after 4 PM ET," with an honest caveat that they "may confirm a few details."

annotations.note: The opening discloses that the agent is automated, gives the inquiry context, and offers the STOP opt-out up front.
"Got it, I'll keep it quick" acknowledges the time pressure, and the agent moves straight to a single ballpark question without commenting on the 7.25% rate.
The agent picked up the balance the borrower volunteered in [3] and didn't re-ask for it; it then skipped the credit question after [5].
The agent assumed "4 PM ET" without confirming the borrower's time zone, which risks a mistimed call.
The close confirms the time, who will call, and how, and avoids overpromising by noting the loan officer "may confirm a few details."

judge.overall_notes: This was a clean, efficient intake that respected a busy borrower, collected all fields, and made no rate or approval implications. The only gaps are that the callback option was never explicitly offered in response to the busy objection and that the time zone was assumed.
